newsitem.title: USA: Tribune Co. posts higher profits.
newsitem.headline: Tribune Co. posts higher profits.

text.p: Tribune Co., the publisher of the Chicago Tribune, said Friday its earnings rose strongly in the fourth quarter due to solid gains in its broadcasting, publishing and education operations.

The company, which owns radio and television stations and the Chicago Cubs baseball team, said its earnings rose to $82 million, or 63 cents a share, in the fourth quarter from $65 million, or 47 cents a share, a year earlier.
Revenues rose 2 percent to $608 million from $594 million.

"These are strong headlines, especially for a company that's positioning itself in higher-growth businesses. At the same time, we are implementing programmes to increase shareholder value," Tribune Chairman John Madigan said in a statement.
"We have great plans for the year ahead with the anticipated February closing of the $1 billion Renaissance acquisition," he said.
In July, the Chicago-based company agreed to acquire Renaissance Communications Corp., which owns six television stations. The deal is expected to close next month.

The company, which owns and operates 10 television and five radio stations, said its broadcasting and entertainment operating profit was up 24 percent to $54 million in the fourth quarter due primarily to improvements in television and at Tribune Entertainment.

Publishing operating profit was up 17 percent to $84 million due mainly to lower newsprint costs. Newsprint and ink expense decreased 27 percent, as average newsprint prices were down about 22 percent from last year.
Tribune publishes four daily newspapers and said operating profit from papers rose 20 percent from last year.

The company, which also provides educational products and services for the school and consumer markets, said its education operations reported a fourth-quarter operating profit of $1.6 million compared with a loss of $2.1 million in 1995.
For all of 1996, Tribune said its overall net income rose 15 percent to $283 million from $245 million in 1995. Earnings per share rose to $2.15 from $1.75.
Revenues rose 7 percent to $2.4 billion from $2.2 billion.
Tribune stock slipped 12.5 cents to $37 in morning trading on the New York Stock Exchange.
